verifications.claim: Section 4 of the 25th Amendment provides a constitutional mechanism for the Vice President and a majority of the Cabinet to declare the President incapacitated and unable to discharge their duties.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Whenever the Vice President and a majority of either the principal officers of the executive departments... transmit... that the President is unable to discharge the powers and duties of his office'; R2: 'Section 4... provides a mechanism for the Vice President and a majority of the principal officers of the executive departments (the Cabinet) to declare that the president is unable to discharge the powers and duties of his office'; R4: 'Section 4... whereby a presidential disability is declared by the Vice President and a majority of the Cabinet'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly quote or paraphrase the exact mechanism described in the claim.

verifications.claim: Section 4 of the 25th Amendment has never been used.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'To date, Section 4 has not been implemented'; R6: 'Section 4, which has never been invoked'; R8: 'Section 4... which has never been invoked'
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements in multiple sources confirm it has never been used.

verifications.claim: Upon such a declaration under Section 4 of the 25th Amendment, the Vice President immediately becomes Acting President.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'the Vice President shall immediately assume the powers and duties of the office as Acting President'; R2: 'the Vice President immediately becomes Acting President and assumes full presidential powers'; R4: 'the Vice President immediately assumes the powers and duties of the office as Acting President'
verifications.reasoning: Exact wording from constitutional text and explanations in sources.

verifications.claim: Under Section 4 of the 25th Amendment, the Vice President and a majority of the principal officers of the executive departments (Cabinet) submit a written declaration to Congress.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'transmit to the President pro tempore of the Senate and the Speaker of the House of Representatives their written declaration'; R2: 'send a written declaration to Congress'; R4: 'transmit a written message to this effect to the President pro tem and the Speaker'
verifications.reasoning: Sources precisely describe the written declaration process to congressional leaders.

verifications.claim: Under Section 4 of the 25th Amendment, the Vice President immediately assumes the powers of the Presidency.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'the Vice President shall immediately assume the powers and duties of the office as Acting President'; R2: 'the vice president immediately becomes Acting President and assumes full presidential powers'; R4: 'the Vice President immediately assumes the powers and duties of the office as Acting President'
verifications.reasoning: Direct support for immediate assumption of presidential powers.

verifications.claim: Under Section 4 of the 25th Amendment, the President can submit a written declaration to Congress stating no disability exists, allowing them to resume duties.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'when the President transmits... his written declaration that no inability exists, he shall resume the powers and duties of his office'; R2: 'The president can contest this by sending his own declaration to Congress stating that he is able to resume his duties'; R4: 'a declaration by the President that the disability invoked... no longer exists'
verifications.reasoning: Sources detail the President's written declaration to resume duties.

verifications.claim: Under Section 4 of the 25th Amendment, if the Vice President and Cabinet dispute the President's return within four days, Congress must meet to decide the matter.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'unless the Vice President and a majority... transmit within four days... Thereupon Congress shall decide the issue, assembling within forty-eight hours'; R2: 'If the president contests it... If the VP and cabinet dispute... Congress must decide the issue within 21 days'; R4: 'the Vice President and the Cabinet or DRB... contest this finding... within four days... Congress decides the issue'
verifications.reasoning: Precise match to the four-day dispute and congressional decision process.

verifications.claim: Under Section 4 of the 25th Amendment, keeping the Vice President as Acting President requires a two-thirds vote in both houses of Congress.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'determines by two-thirds vote of both Houses that the President is unable... the Vice President shall continue... as Acting President'; R2: 'A two-thirds vote in both the House and Senate is required to keep the Vice President as Acting President'; R4: 'If Congress determines by a two-thirds vote... the Vice President continues as Acting President'
verifications.reasoning: Exact description of the two-thirds vote requirement.

verifications.claim: Section 4 of the 25th Amendment was created to address situations where a President is unable to function but cannot or will not transfer power voluntarily.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'designed to deal with a situation where an incapacitated President couldn’t tell Congress that the Vice President needed to act as President'; R4: 'Section 4 assumes that the President... is unable or unwilling to declare an obvious disability'; R7: 'Section 4 addresses... a President who may be unable to fulfill his constitutional role but who cannot or will not step aside'; R6: 'when the President is unable or unwilling to declare that he is incapacitated'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state the purpose as handling involuntary incapacity.

verifications.claim: Sections 1-3 of the 25th Amendment address death, resignation, or voluntary transfer.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Sections 1 & 2: Succession' (death, resignation); 'Section 3... allows the President to tell Congress that the Vice President can act as President'; R3: Sec1 'removal... death or resignation'; Sec3 voluntary declaration; R7: Sec1 presidential vacancies (death/resignation); Sec3 voluntary transfer; R8: Sec1 permanent (death etc.); Sec3 temporary voluntary
verifications.reasoning: Sources group Sec1-2 as succession (death/resignation), Sec3 as voluntary disability transfer.

verifications.claim: Section 4 of the 25th Amendment deals exclusively with involuntary transfer of power due to illness or incapacity.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Sections 3 and 4 deal with... disability'; Sec4 'most controversial... Vice President and... Cabinet... jointly agree that the President is unable'; R4: 'Section 4: Contingent Disability... activated only in response to a presidential disability... President... unable or unwilling'; R6: 'Section 4... to initiate the transfer... when the President is unable or unwilling'; R7: 'Section 4 addresses the dramatic case... cannot or will not step aside'
verifications.reasoning: Directly contrasted with voluntary Sec3; 'exclusively' aligns with descriptions as involuntary mechanism.

verifications.claim: In Section 4 of the 25th Amendment, "principal officers" generally refers to Cabinet members.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'the Cabinet consists of "the principal officers of the executive departments"'; R6: '"principal officers" are members of the President’s official Cabinet'; R7: 'principal officers of the executive departments... only Cabinet members ought to count'
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently equate 'principal officers' with Cabinet members.

verifications.claim: Whether "acting" secretaries can vote under Section 4 of the 25th Amendment is debated.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: '"the acting head (of a Cabinet department) would be authorized..." Senate debate... questioned by some Senators'; R5: 'Less clear is whether acting Cabinet members count... present scholarly consensus... this Essay complicates that consensus'; R6: 'for various views as to whether acting Cabinet Secretaries may participate...'; R7: 'what to do with Cabinet members serving in an "acting"... capacity'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly note debate or uncertainty on acting secretaries.
